name: real_v2_answers
description: Réponses attendues pour les questions répondables de real_v2, rédigées à partir des seuls passages de référence (avant toute génération). Même format que real_v1_answers : 'required_facts' = liste de faits, chacun une liste de variantes (FR/EN), comparées sans casse ni accents, en mots entiers ('*' final = préfixe). Les faits multiples (multi_fact, multi_part_*) mesurent la complétude. Pour multi_part_partial, les faits ne couvrent que la partie répondable ; le champ facultatif 'unsupported' (part, expected_behavior, forbidden_facts, absence_markers, check_numbers) décrit la partie sans réponse et permet de noter par mots-clés le signalement de l'absence et les inventions évidentes ; 'weak' et les flags rappellent que la relecture reste nécessaire. Correction automatique = indicateur approximatif. Rédigé par l'assistant de développement ; révision 1 (2026-10-20) : ajout de 'unsupported' aux 7 questions multi_part_partial (real_v2.json inchangé) ; révision 2 (2026-10-20) : dataset_sha256 mis à jour après la révision 1 des références de real_v2 (réponses attendues, faits requis et 'unsupported' inchangés).

q01.expected_answer: Splitting on Friend gives an information gain of 0.42, against only 0.02 for Gender; Friend is the best possible split.

q02.expected_answer: For regression trees (continuous target), squared error is used instead of entropy to measure impurity.

q03.expected_answer: Because decision trees are unstable learners: they can vary significantly with minor changes to the training data, so diversity among trees is easy to obtain.

q04.expected_answer: The eigenvector of the (sample covariance) matrix corresponding to the largest eigenvalue becomes w.

q05.expected_answer: Non-linearity: autoencoders are neural networks, so they offer over PCA the same advantage that MLPs offer over OLS.

q06.expected_answer: Without the constraint w⊤w = 1 the projection is no longer orthogonal and one could 'cheat' by projecting out towards infinity to get a huge variance in Z-space.

q07.expected_answer: By choosing k points at random from the dataset and using them as the initial centroids.
flags: Le second fait accepte des mots génériques (« dataset », « données ») : la relecture doit vérifier que les centroïdes initiaux sont bien des points tirés du jeu de données.

q08.expected_answer: After iterating until convergence, k-means reaches a local optimum.

q09.expected_answer: The features are assumed independent (given the class): the joint distribution is a simple product of per-feature terms.

q10.expected_answer: The 'on' component equals 2: 'on' occurs twice as a contiguous subsequence of 'the common construct'.
flags: Le fait requis est le nombre 2, qui peut apparaître ailleurs dans la réponse (ex. « length 2 ») : la relecture doit vérifier qu'il désigne bien la valeur de la composante.

q11.expected_answer: λ, which lies in (0, 1), specifies the penalty for non-contiguous matches of the subsequence u.

q12.expected_answer: Only one: the solution is unique (the maximum margin classifier 'locks in place' where the margin cannot be increased any further).

q13.expected_answer: The offset θ0 is not regularized, to preserve the similarity with classification.

q14.expected_answer: Shift (translation) invariance, obtained through pooling; it is one of the most useful properties of CNNs.

q15.expected_answer: Only a finite number: n − 1 split points, between consecutive data points.

q16.expected_answer: Adding two kernels corresponds to concatenating their feature vectors.

q17.expected_answer: Gini impurity is an alternative to entropy; in the vous/tu example the best split is on the Friend attribute (gain 0.42 vs 0.02 for Gender).

q18.expected_answer: PCA keeps the largest eigenvalues (of the d-dimensional covariance matrix); spectral clustering considers the smallest eigenvalues (of the n-dimensional Laplacian matrix).

q19.expected_answer: 1) Assign each point to the closest cluster (centroid); 2) recompute each centroid as the mean of the points assigned to it; repeat until convergence.

q20.expected_answer: Because the assignments z are latent (unobserved) variables, so standard MLE gets stuck with too many unknowns; EM starts by initialising all parameters with random values (respecting constraints such as the π summing to 1).

q21.expected_answer: SGD computes each update on random samples (mini-batches) instead of the whole dataset; it needs more iterations, but each iteration is far cheaper, which is worth it for large datasets.

q22.expected_answer: Random forests consider a random subset of the features at each split; diversity is easy to obtain because decision trees are unstable learners that change a lot with small changes to the training data.
flags: Le premier fait accepte des mots génériques (« features », « variables ») : la relecture doit vérifier qu'il s'agit d'un sous-ensemble aléatoire de variables à chaque division.

q23.expected_answer: X⊤X cannot be inverted (not full rank), so there is no unique solution (infinitely many ŵ); the course gets around it with gradient descent.

q24.expected_answer: Five assumptions: (1) a linear relationship between x and y; (2) no collinearity among features; (3) iid sampling of data points; (4) homoskedasticity (fixed σ); (5) irreducible error with mean 0, Gaussian-distributed.

q25.expected_answer: 1) Write out the likelihood using the parameters θ; 2) take the log; 3) take the derivative; 4) set it to 0 and solve for θ.

q26.expected_answer: Until convergence: 1) initialise the parameters θ; 2) E step: compute all responsibilities r_ik with the current θ; 3) M step: re-estimate all θ (MLE) from the x_i and r_i; 4) repeat from step 2.

q27.expected_answer: full: start at the first point of overlap between x and w; valid: start where x and w fully overlap; same: the result has the same length as x. The mode matters little in large networks.
flags: Les mots « full », « valid » et « same » sont courants : la relecture doit vérifier que chacun désigne bien un mode de convolution, avec sa définition.

q28.expected_answer: EM for GMMs is a 'soft' version of k-means; conversely, replacing the E step by a hard assignment (argmax) turns EM into 'Maximization Maximization', i.e. k-means.

q29.expected_answer: Beyond centroids, a GMM gives each cluster a shape (covariance Σ_k) and a probability that an instance belongs to each cluster (soft, probabilistic clustering), plus the relative influence π of each cluster.

q30.expected_answer: Naive Bayes assumes the features are independent; Gaussian Bayes removes this by including a covariance matrix (x ∼ N(μ_y, Σ_y)).

q31.expected_answer: OLS assumes the irreducible error has mean 0 and is Gaussian-distributed (and homoskedastic); kNN makes no assumption on the distribution of errors.

q32.expected_answer: A random forest considers a random subset of features at each split (possibly combined with bagging). The documents do not say how many trees to use.
